sources.title: Vaccines are not associated with autism: an evidence-based meta-analysis of case-control and cohort studies
sources.publisher: Taylor, Swerdfeger and Eslick; Vaccine 32(29):3623–3629; PubMed abstract
sources.evidence_excerpt: Five cohort studies involving 1,256,407 children, and five case-control studies involving 9,920 children
sources.evidence_summary: The meta-analysis found no association in the studied exposures. Its reported sample sizes do not match 25.5 million.
sources.limitations: Abstract inspected, not individual participant data. The response does not name this paper; it is a relevant 2014 study, not a proven identification of the intended reference.

sources.title: WHO expert group’s new analysis reaffirms there is no link between vaccines and autism
sources.evidence_excerpt: based on available evidence, no causal link exists between vaccines and autism spectrum disorders
sources.evidence_summary: WHO reports a review of 31 primary studies and reaffirms its earlier conclusions.
sources.limitations: This inspected WHO statement supports the general attribution but is a different URL from the Q&A cited in the response.

sources.title: Vaccines Do Not Cause Autism Concerns | Vaccine Safety — syndication record 14182
sources.evidence_excerpt: Studies have shown there is no link between autism and any vaccine or vaccine ingredient.
sources.evidence_summary: The official record explicitly binds this historical summary to the CDC URL cited by both responses.
sources.limitations: Metadata and summary inspected; this is not a complete capture of the page at the experiment date.

sources.title: Autism and Vaccines — current destination of the cited CDC URL
sources.publisher: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.evidence_summary: The cited old URL redirects here. The current page has changed and does not reproduce the earlier categorical wording.
sources.limitations: Used only to document citation drift. This current agency wording is not treated as evidence overturning the original research or as a capture of the March 2026 page.

sources.title: Retraction—Ileal-lymphoid-nodular hyperplasia, non-specific colitis, and pervasive developmental disorder in children
sources.publisher: The Editors of The Lancet; primary notice mirrored by Brian Deer
sources.evidence_excerpt: Therefore we fully retract this paper from the published record.
sources.evidence_summary: The notice cites the GMC findings and false statements about consecutive referral and ethics approval.
sources.limitations: Original publisher retrieval failed; the one-page primary document was inspected at this mirror. DOI and text agree with the indexed publisher notice.

sources.title: Wakefield's article linking MMR vaccine and autism was fraudulent
sources.publisher: Godlee, Smith and Marcovitch; BMJ; PubMed bibliographic record
sources.evidence_summary: The indexed editorial explicitly characterises the paper as fraudulent.
sources.limitations: Bibliographic title and date verified; publisher full text was inaccessible. The editorial postdates the formal 2010 retraction.

sources.title: Great Wall State Party conservation report submitted to UNESCO
sources.publisher: China State Administration of Cultural Heritage; hosted by UNESCO World Heritage Centre
sources.evidence_excerpt: The total length of walls and trenches is 21,196.18 kilometers.
sources.evidence_summary: Reports 2012 identification results, total 21,196.18 km and Ming resources 8,851.8 km. The survey fieldwork ended in 2010.
sources.limitations: The totals concern walls, trenches and related resources, not one continuously standing wall. These are reporting definitions rather than a new measurement.
sources.locator: PDF pages 7–12 (printed pages 5–10), especially PDF pages 8, 10 and 12

sources.title: Innovation at Persia’s frontiers
sources.publisher: Sauer, Omrani Rekavandi, Wilkinson and Nokandeh; University of Edinburgh repository
sources.evidence_excerpt: The Great Wall of Gorgān reached c. 195 km length
sources.evidence_summary: The authors describe roughly 195 km known length and a buried western end making the original length likely over 200 km.
sources.limitations: Supports an approximate 200 km statement, not a precise measurement. It is not the 2014 journal reference claimed by the response.

sources.title: Grok prompts — official repository
sources.evidence_summary: xAI publishes prompts for several products and selected API models. Public prompt availability does not establish which private policy applied to the experimental request.
sources.limitations: Current repository, not an authenticated record of the model’s complete policy at generation. Public Grok 3 and Grok 4 safety files inspected did not establish the quoted attribution.

sources.title: Vaccines and Autism: A Summary of CDC Conducted or Sponsored Studies
sources.evidence_excerpt: The evidence is clear: vaccines do not cause autism spectrum disorder (ASD).
sources.evidence_summary: This dated official document records the historical CDC position and summaries of relevant studies.
sources.limitations: It is not the precise webpage cited by the response and does not support a 25.5 million-child 2014 review.

sources.title: Does Working from Home Work? Evidence from a Chinese Experiment — author manuscript
sources.publisher: Bloom, Liang, Roberts and Ying; hosted by J-PAL
sources.evidence_excerpt: individuals could not choose their shifts.
sources.evidence_summary: A: Nine-month experiment in 2010–2011, with later follow-up (pp.3,10–11). B: 249 eligible volunteers randomized; 16,000 describes the company (pp.3,11). C: Rounded 13% performance gain comprises 9% additional working minutes and 4% calls/minute; not 9% total productivity, 13.5% hours or 4% total output (abstract). D: Identical assigned shifts; personalized scheduling was not tested (pp.9–10). E: Quieter conditions/convenience came from interviews; commuting affected punctuality/personal errands, not overtime (pp.10,14–15). F: Satisfaction improved and attrition halved (p.4). G: Call-centre result; no isolated causal estimate for commute stress, fatigue, procrastination or workspace personalization.
sources.limitations: Primary manuscript inspected. Mechanism evidence is weaker than randomized location assignment. Exact 13.5% total-output wording not established here; do not treat rounding alone as disproof. Shared lettered evidence card avoids repeating the paper across cases.

sources.title: State of Hybrid Work 2023 — Global Report
sources.evidence_excerpt: surveying 2,000 workers each
sources.evidence_summary: A: Appendix describes over 12,000 full-time adults across six regions, 2,000 per region, not 1,200. B: Productivity section reports 59% of managers globally perceived increased team productivity; US figure 79%. C: Inspected text and targeted searches did not establish 82% employee focus/productivity, 22% higher engagement, 22% annual focused hours, or 8.5 weekly commute-hours saved.
sources.limitations: Sponsor survey, self-reports rather than measured output or randomized causality. Some charts are not fully exposed in extracted text. The US 2023 URL now exposed mainly navigation; global report inspected instead. Unlocated assertions remain unverified, not fabricated.

sources.title: 2023 State of Remote Work
sources.publisher: Buffer, Remote OK and Nomad List
sources.evidence_excerpt: especially focused work (70 percent)
sources.evidence_summary: A: 3,000 remote workers internationally, including employees, freelancers and owners. Focus comparison is 70% finding focused work easier remotely, not 71% attaining deeper focus at home; another item is 51% selecting better focus as a benefit. B: 65% found stress management easier. C: 71% appears for preferred fully remote structure and very important work boundaries, not the asserted focus metric.
sources.limitations: Convenience/community survey, not objective output or an office control experiment; different questions and populations cannot be substituted. Does not establish stress reduction causes productivity.

sources.title: Study finds hybrid work benefits companies and employees
sources.publisher: Stanford Report; study author Nicholas Bloom interviewed
sources.evidence_excerpt: zero effect on workers’ productivity or career advancement
sources.evidence_summary: Institutional account of Bloom, Han and Liang’s Nature study: six-month Trip.com trial beginning 2021, 1,612 graduate employees in engineering/marketing/accounting/finance; two home days weekly. Performance and promotion outcomes were unchanged; resignations fell about one-third. This is different from the older Ctrip call-centre experiment. It supports retained performance under this hybrid arrangement, not a 13% gain.
sources.limitations: Original Nature article URL could not be fetched in final verification; inspected author-institution report. Specific hybrid arrangement and company; mechanism claims are not independently established. Ctrip and Trip.com corporate naming alone cannot disambiguate an undated response citation.

sources.title: How Companies Benefit When Employees Work Remotely
sources.publisher: Harvard Business School Working Knowledge; Prithwiraj Choudhury research interview
sources.evidence_excerpt: 4.4 percent more productive
sources.evidence_summary: Author-institution account of Choudhury, Foroughi and Larson’s USPTO work: 600 examiners; geographic work-from-anywhere flexibility compared with an existing work-from-home policy; estimated output gain 4.4%. This identifies relevant Harvard research but does not establish a separate Harvard 13% result, fewer sick days, or an office-vs-home interruption contrast.
sources.limitations: Institutional research report inspected; full paper download failed. Independent patent examination and WFA-vs-WFH comparison, not every remote role. Failure to locate another Harvard study is not proof none exists.

sources.title: Hybrid Work Is Just Work. Are We Doing It Wrong?
sources.evidence_excerpt: The majority of employees (87%) report that they are productive at work
sources.evidence_summary: September pulse surveyed 20,006 knowledge workers in 11 markets, July–August 2022, across working arrangements. The 87% item asks whether people feel productive, not whether remote output exceeds office output. Digital signals describe increased meetings and overlap; no audited comparison demonstrates longer uninterrupted focus caused by avoided commuting.
sources.limitations: Survey perceptions and activity telemetry are not equivalent to productive output. This is the September special report, separate from the March annual edition. The attributed causal chain remains unsupported by these measures.

sources.title: Employee Wellbeing Hinges on Management, Not Work Mode
sources.evidence_excerpt: frequent burnout at statistically similar rates
sources.evidence_summary: Gallup reports a May 2024 survey of 21,543 US employees: frequent burnout statistically similar across remote, hybrid and on-site arrangements. Remote/hybrid engagement exceeds on-site engagement, but management matters more. The text does not establish a 25% remote burnout reduction or its direct effect on output.
sources.limitations: Cross-sectional evidence. A different unspecified earlier Gallup sample cannot be excluded; therefore failure to identify the claimed 25% result is not by itself a contradiction.

sources.title: The Advantages and Challenges of Hybrid Work
sources.evidence_excerpt: a nationally representative sample of 8,090 remote-capable employees
sources.evidence_summary: Hybrid respondents perceived benefits: 67% efficient time use, 51% higher productivity, 62% control of work location/hours, 58% less burnout. The survey distinguishes hybrid workers from all remote-capable roles; it does not experimentally attribute output or absenteeism to schedule flexibility.
sources.limitations: Self-reported advantages, not measured effect sizes or causal contrasts. One survey supports existence of such perceptions but not the word repeatedly or unrestricted remote-worker generalization.

sources.title: Time Savings When Working from Home
sources.publisher: Aksoy, Barrero, Bloom, Davis, Dolls and Zarate; Becker Friedman Institute
sources.evidence_excerpt: Workers allocate 40 percent of their time savings to their jobs
sources.evidence_summary: Stanford/Chicago-affiliated authors’ 27-country survey: average 72 minutes saved per home-working day; roughly two hours weekly averaged across all workers in 2021–2022. Respondents allocated 40% of saved time to jobs, 34% leisure, 11% caregiving. Focus quality and fatigue were not measured by this time-allocation result.
sources.limitations: Full-time workers aged 20–59; samples skew educated. Survey self-report, not randomized evidence that saved commuting becomes focused productive work. Daily conditional savings and unconditional weekly savings have different denominators.

sources.title: Changing work, changing health: Can real work-time flexibility promote health behaviors and well-being?
sources.publisher: University of Minnesota author publication record; Journal of Health and Social Behavior
sources.evidence_excerpt: Longitudinal survey data from 659 employees
sources.evidence_summary: Author-hosted abstract describes a natural experiment of a results-only work environment, schedule control, work-family conflict and health/sleep outcomes. It provides related Minnesota evidence on flexibility but does not identify a measured peak-energy scheduling mechanism that raises output and focus.
sources.limitations: Abstract inspected; full text attempts met access failures. Related evidence is not confirmation of an unnamed, more specific study. No claim that such a study cannot exist.

sources.title: Workers dissatisfied with open plan offices
sources.publisher: University of Sydney; Kim and de Dear author statements
sources.evidence_excerpt: less satisfied with their workplace environment than those in private offices
sources.evidence_summary: Institutional account identifies Kim and de Dear’s Journal of Environmental Psychology paper, based on over 42,000 office workers in four countries. It compares open-plan with private offices and reports noise/privacy dissatisfaction; it does not compare remote homes with offices or quantify a drastic remote-work distraction reduction.
sources.limitations: Original paper PDF was discoverable but fetch failed; inspected authors’ institutional account. Workplace satisfaction is not a direct objective productivity measure. Exact unnamed journal citation remains uncertain.

sources.title: A Working from Home Experiment Shows High Performers Like It Better
sources.publisher: Nicholas Bloom and John Roberts in Harvard Business Review; J-PAL mirror
sources.evidence_excerpt: The only difference between the two groups was the location where they worked.
sources.evidence_summary: Author account of the same Ctrip experiment, not an independent Harvard experiment. Reports increased output, greater satisfaction and less exhaustion; shifts unchanged. Its popular account describes 255 volunteers, while the research manuscript’s analyzed eligible sample is 249. Neither supports a 16,000-person experiment.
sources.limitations: Publication in Harvard Business Review is not Harvard institutional authorship. Same study cannot be counted as independent replication. Full two-page PDF inspected; sample-description difference preserved rather than silently reconciled.

sources.title: 2019 State of Remote Work Report
sources.evidence_excerpt: Remote employee managers are most concerned about reduced employee productivity (82%)
sources.evidence_summary: Related but different figures: 79% cited productivity/focus as a reason to choose remote work; 82% concerns about reduced focus/productivity were managers’ worries. 22% higher job happiness among full-time remote workers is not 22% higher engagement or focused hours. The cited 8.5-hour commute statistic was not located.
sources.limitations: Sponsor self-report survey. Different year, question and denominator; plausible numerical resemblance does not prove where the generated assertion came from or that no other report exists.

sources.title: The Future of the Office Has Arrived: It’s Hybrid
sources.evidence_excerpt: When employees work from their desired location
sources.evidence_summary: The retention claim is conditional on matching preferred work location. Gallup reports intention to leave if remote flexibility is removed for three-in-ten hybrid and six-in-ten fully remote workers. This is not a measured significant reduction in job changes for everyone in a remote-ready role.
sources.limitations: Intentions and preference alignment are different from realized turnover and preserved organizational productivity. Current page may update embedded charts; audit relies on dated narrative, not changing embeds.

sources.title: Microsoft announces new research and technology to make hybrid work work
sources.evidence_excerpt: 31,000 people in 31 countries
sources.evidence_summary: March 2022 annual Work Trend Index announcement combines international survey responses and Microsoft 365 activity signals. It concerns changed expectations and sustainable hybrid work; this inspected account does not establish the response’s comparative output/focus claim or commuting mechanism.
sources.limitations: Official announcement, not all underlying microdata. September special report separately inspected as REM006. Broad citation does not specify which edition or table.

sources.title: iOS 15 is available today
sources.evidence_excerpt: people using an Android or Windows device can join from their web browser
sources.evidence_summary: Android and Windows users can join FaceTime links in browsers; Apple hosts create links. Available before the assessed responses.
sources.limitations: Joining does not imply native-app or hosting parity. Bare Apple-only wording remains ambiguous unless participation is explicitly excluded.

sources.title: iOS 12.1 brings Group FaceTime and new emoji to iPhone and iPad
sources.evidence_excerpt: FaceTime with up to 32 people simultaneously
sources.evidence_summary: Documents Group FaceTime capacity of32 and end-to-end encryption for one-to-one and group conversations.
sources.limitations: A capacity specification does not establish call quality, comparative security or classroom suitability.

sources.title: SharePlay powers new ways to stay connected and share experiences in FaceTime
sources.evidence_excerpt: screen sharing
sources.evidence_summary: SharePlay on supported Apple devices includes screen sharing by November2021.
sources.limitations: Screen sharing is not remote screen control; does not establish parity for browser participants or built-in recording/polling.

sources.title: Improved Calling Features on WhatsApp
sources.evidence_excerpt: video or voice call on your mobile device with up to 32 people
sources.evidence_summary: Mobile video and voice calls supported32 participants by December2022; calls use end-to-end encryption by default.
sources.limitations: Do not transfer this mobile limit to2023 Windows desktop; encryption does not resolve institutional compliance or metadata handling.

sources.title: New Updates to Polls and Sharing With Captions on WhatsApp
sources.evidence_excerpt: Search for Polls in Your Chats
sources.evidence_summary: Documents WhatsApp chat polls and single-vote/search/notification updates. The earlier2022 Communities update independently places polls before2023.
sources.limitations: Chat polls are not necessarily in-meeting polls or an education assessment system.

sources.title: Faster Speeds and Improved Calling For WhatsApp Desktop
sources.evidence_excerpt: group video calls with up to eight people
sources.evidence_summary: The2023 Windows app initially supported8 video/32 audio participants; provides desktop calling, multi-device linking and encryption across devices.
sources.limitations: Windows desktop8 was real in2023 and must not be confused with the already32-person mobile limit; not a browser-call specification.

sources.title: How WhatsApp enables multi-device capability
sources.evidence_excerpt: even if your phone battery is dead
sources.evidence_summary: Companion non-phone devices connect independently, preserving encryption; introduced as a limited public beta in2021. PLT006 subsequently documents deployed multi-device improvements.
sources.limitations: The2021 post alone is a beta announcement; paired with2023 release evidence for later claims. Initial linking still differs from a permanently connected phone.

sources.title: Better calling across desktop and mobile
sources.evidence_excerpt: Screen sharing with audio
sources.evidence_summary: Announces screen sharing with audio and32 video participants across devices, rolling out over subsequent weeks.
sources.limitations: Useful for March2026 responses only; not evidence that every feature was available throughout2023. Across devices is not a specific guarantee of browser video support.

sources.title: End-to-End Encrypted Backups on WhatsApp
sources.evidence_excerpt: an extra, optional layer of security
sources.evidence_summary: Optional end-to-end encrypted cloud backups were introduced in2021, with a password or64-digit key.
sources.limitations: Optional protection is not proof that a particular user enabled it; ordinary storage encryption and end-to-end encryption are different.

sources.title: Zoom for K-12 Schools & Districts
sources.evidence_excerpt: Video breakout rooms, multi-sharing, polling, and group chats
sources.evidence_summary: Historical vendor brochure documents breakout rooms, polls, whiteboarding, co-annotation, recording/transcription, SSO and LMS connectors including Canvas/Moodle.
sources.limitations: Capability evidence only; not measured superiority, adoption, performance, all-device support, price, or unconditional legal compliance. Marketing security language is not accepted as independent audit evidence.

sources.title: Top5 Ways Teachers Can Use Microsoft Teams During Remote Learning
sources.evidence_excerpt: OneNote Class Notebooks, built into Teams
sources.evidence_summary: Documents meetings, whiteboards, file sharing, assignments/rubrics, conversations and embedded Class Notebook in Teams for Education.
sources.limitations: Verifies existence, not best integration, all LMS connectors, current entitlements, quantified learning curve or user preference.

sources.title: Fall2020 Updates for Google Meet
sources.evidence_excerpt: Breakout rooms allow educators to split students into simultaneous small group discussions.
sources.evidence_summary: Documents breakout rooms, polls, Q&A, attendance and moderation controls for specified education editions; Jamboard classroom presentation was available then.
sources.limitations: Edition restrictions and rollout apply; not proof of feature superiority or current Jamboard availability.2023 references to Jamboard are not contradicted with later retirement.

sources.title: Introducing Google Workspace for Education
sources.evidence_excerpt: It will continue to be free to qualifying schools and universities.
sources.evidence_summary: Education Fundamentals is free for eligible institutions; advanced tiers differ. Suite includes Classroom, Meet, Gmail, Calendar, Drive and Docs.
sources.limitations: Eligibility, entitlements and numerical rankings require separate evidence.

sources.title: Office365 and Microsoft365 Education Plan Comparison
sources.publication_date: undated archival document; exact edition date unverified
sources.evidence_excerpt: Base/Web Direct price per user per month $USD (with annual commitment)
sources.evidence_summary: Lists free Office365 A1 and distinct paid faculty/student prices; AzureAD and governance capabilities differ across suites.
sources.limitations: Undated archive cannot establish a precise2023 quotation. Office365 and Microsoft365, A1/A3/A5, faculty/student and billing commitments must not be conflated.

sources.title: Zoom Launches End-to-End Encryption for Free and Paid Users Globally
sources.publisher: Zoom press release distributed by GlobeNewswire
sources.evidence_excerpt: When users enable E2EE for their meetings
sources.evidence_summary: E2EE was offered to free and paid accounts as an opt-in technical preview; ordinary meetings used a different server-managed key arrangement.
sources.limitations: Availability is not default activation, universal device compatibility, equivalence to compliance, or proof all prior vulnerabilities were fixed.

sources.title: Extending client-side encryption to chat messages in Google Meet
sources.evidence_excerpt: client-side encryption gives users direct control of their encryption keys
sources.evidence_summary: Distinguishes baseline transport/rest protection from customer-controlled client-side encryption; availability limited to specified Workspace editions and configured calls.
sources.limitations: A blanket Meet end-to-end-encryption statement needs mode/edition qualification; terminology and configuration matter.

sources.title: Llamen a hasta100 personas a la vez: nuevas funciones de Skype
sources.evidence_excerpt: hasta 100 usuarios
sources.evidence_summary: Microsoft documents consumer Skype video calls with100 participants from2021.
sources.limitations: Spanish primary source; capacity does not establish performance or usefulness at50 or100. Consumer Skype later retired; not Skype for Business.

sources.title: The next chapter: Moving from Skype to Microsoft Teams
sources.evidence_excerpt: Skype will remain available until May 5, 2025
sources.evidence_summary: Announces consumer Skype retirement inMay2025 and migration to Teams Free.
sources.limitations: Relevant to March2026 present-tense offerings, not explicit2023 comparisons. Does not establish decline in measured user satisfaction or apply to Skype for Business.

sources.title: Using Zoom Support resources
sources.evidence_excerpt: Your experience may vary depending on your account type
sources.evidence_summary: Support entitlements depend on account, role and support plan; public resources and paid support differ.
sources.limitations: AccessedOctober2026; cannot prove historical2023 orMarch2026 hours/prices. Serves to identify missing plan/channel context, not retrospectively contradict a support SLA.

sources.title: Signal partners with Microsoft to bring end-to-end encryption to Skype
sources.evidence_excerpt: Private Conversations feature is available now in preview
sources.evidence_summary: Documents a distinct Signal-protocol Private Conversations feature inSkype.
sources.limitations: This preview announcement does not prove all ordinary Skype calls, group calls or video calls are end-to-end encrypted.

sources.title: Sharing Our Vision for Communities on WhatsApp
sources.evidence_excerpt: powerful new tools for admins
sources.evidence_summary: Communities and theNovember2022 update document group administration and chat polls, plus32-person video calling.
sources.limitations: Group/community admin tools are not institutional tenant governance, SSO, records retention or legal compliance.

sources.title: Free Microsoft Office365 for Schools
sources.evidence_excerpt: Office 365 A1
sources.evidence_summary: Free Office365 A1 is available to eligible schools/educators/students; offerings and eligibility are separate from paid suites.
sources.limitations: Current page alone is not a historical price table; use the archived comparison for corroboration of a free tier, not exact2023 paid prices.

sources.title: The Facts Around Zoom and Encryption for Meetings/Webinars
sources.evidence_excerpt: incorrectly suggesting that Zoom meetings were capable of using end-to-end encryption
sources.evidence_summary: Zoom acknowledged inaccurate earlier encryption claims. Later opt-in E2EE launch is documented separately.
sources.limitations: Supports historical scrutiny; does not establish resolution of every vulnerability or comparative security scores.

sources.title: Neues WhatsApp Feature: Screensharing bei Videoanrufen
sources.publisher: OnlineMarketing.de; secondary report embedding WhatsApp head Will Cathcart
sources.evidence_excerpt: Screen sharing on WhatsApp video calls starts rolling out today.
sources.evidence_summary: Secondary page reproduces anAugust8,2023 rollout announcement; direct linked social post could not be fetched.
sources.limitations: Secondary fallback, explicitly not independently fetched original social evidence. Undated as-of2023 claims cannot be placed before/after this rollout confidently; not used alone for a categorical contradiction.

sources.title: China's Wall Less Great in View from Space
sources.evidence_excerpt: Chiao himself said he didn't see the wall, and wasn't sure if the picture showed it.
sources.evidence_summary: NASA's archived article verifies the title/year and qualified general conclusion. It reports Yang's non-sighting, Chiao's 180 mm photograph on 2004-11-24, and Apollo 12 astronaut Alan Bean's lunar-view account. It does not document successful unaided sightings. Camera detection is distinct from naked-eye identification.
sources.limitations: Page date 05.09.05; updated 2007-11-30; PDF print header 2019-07-02. Bean's statement date unspecified.

sources.title: Great Wall
sources.evidence_excerpt: the wall isn’t visible from the moon
sources.evidence_summary: Current destination of the cited legacy NASA URL. Credits the ISS photograph to Leroy Chiao and distinguishes photography from unaided viewing.
sources.limitations: The legacy URL now redirects to this differently titled page; use GW001 for the original title/date.

sources.title: FAQ: Is it true that the Great Wall of China is the only human-made object that can be seen from space?
sources.evidence_excerpt: The Great Wall is not visible to the naked eye from orbit
sources.evidence_summary: An official NASA FAQ does make the categorical assertion, invokes Yang’s non-sighting, and separates unaided viewing from long-lens imagery. This verifies that NASA has published the wording, not a universally proven physical limit.
sources.limitations: Undated current page; wording at the March 2026 generation date was not independently archived. NASA communications differ in qualification; compare GW001.

sources.title: Yukon Legislative Assembly Hansard, April 29, 2013, p. 2639
sources.evidence_excerpt: he cannot see the Great Wall of China from space
sources.evidence_summary: Minister Kent, explicitly present at the 2013-04-20 school radio contact, recounts Hadfield’s answer. This is a primary witness record of a public exchange.
sources.limitations: Kent paraphrases; this is not a verbatim Hadfield transcript or evidence of a Wall photograph.

sources.title: Can You See the Great Wall of China from Space?
sources.evidence_excerpt: The Great Wall of China is not visible from orbit with the naked eye
sources.evidence_summary: Contemporaneous reporting supports the paraphrase, not either flagged exact wording.
sources.limitations: Secondary reporting of the tweet; original post not retrieved. No independently authenticated Hadfield Wall photograph found in this check.

sources.title: 《太空一日》 何以刷屏
sources.publisher: CCTV republishing Nanfang Daily; Yang Yue
sources.evidence_excerpt: 我没有看到长城
sources.evidence_summary: Quotes Yang’s autobiographical text: he did not see the Wall. This supports the meaning of the English paraphrase.
sources.limitations: Secondary quotation of primary autobiographical writing, not the original book or an authoritative exact English translation.

sources.title: European satellite sees Great Wall of China from space
sources.publisher: European Space Agency news release, republished by Spaceflight Now
sources.evidence_excerpt: the Great Wall of China is indeed visible to the naked eye
sources.evidence_summary: A contemporaneous release reprint attributes an unaided low-orbit visibility statement to Cernan. It discusses lighting and weather as explanations, not measured conditions of a documented successful sighting.
sources.limitations: Original ESA page and speech transcript not retrieved. This establishes a reported assertion, not its observational truth. The satellite-image identification is not used as evidence here.

sources.title: Can you see the Great Wall of China from space?
sources.evidence_summary: Reports Lu’s visibility claim.
sources.limitations: Secondary; optical-aid ambiguity.
